piece_type: DTC broadcast TV ad ('January 2026 Pill Spot')
regs_in_letter: FD&C Act misbranding (false or misleading); no CFR section cited in letter text

cases.claim: VO: “The first and only FDA approved GLP-1 weight loss pill.” ON-SCREEN TEXT: “Only GLP-1 weight-loss pill” | VO: “Weight loss has never looked like this.” | VO: “The power of Wegovy, now in the palm of your hand.” | VO: “Weight loss with Wegovy isn’t a shortcut. It's a way forward.”
cases.context: Efficacy from placebo-controlled trial only; no data showing superiority to other GLP-1s. Letter text is OCR (e.g., 'Meet Wegovy?® pill').
cases.rationale: Implies pill form offers superior efficacy/safety and outcomes not previously possible.
cases.check: Does novelty of dosage form ('first', 'only', 'never looked like this') imply superior efficacy/safety without head-to-head data?

cases.claim: VO: “Now you can live lighter by losing weight.” ON-SCREEN TEXT: “LIVE LIGHTER™ by losing weight” | VO: “Live lighter by losing weight and keeping it off.” ON-SCREEN TEXT: “LIVE LIGHTER™ by losing weight and keeping it off”
cases.rationale: Implies additional weight loss vs other GLP-1s and emotional/psychological benefits not demonstrated.
cases.check: Do slogans imply emotional, psychological, or life-direction benefits beyond the labeled clinical effect?

cases.cat: Major statement not in dual modality (TV)
cases.claim: The major statement includes presentations where there is information in the SUPERs that is not from the corresponding audio.
cases.check: Rule: SUPER text during the major statement must match the audio.
